expectations.text: Frames the relationship correctly: the Essential Eight is a prioritised set of mitigation strategies aligned with a subset of ISM controls — E8 maturity work complements but does not substitute for broader ISM compliance and authorisation
expectations.evidence: 'The Essential Eight is a prioritised set of eight mitigation strategies... The Essential Eight is not the entirety of the ISM — the ISM covers many additional areas... The Essential Eight specifically targets the mitigations... most effective against common intrusion techniques.'

expectations.text: Names all eight strategies correctly: application control, patch applications, configure Microsoft Office macro settings, user application hardening, restrict administrative privileges, patch operating systems, multi-factor authentication, regular backups
expectations.evidence: Mapping table and ML2 section list all eight strategies exactly as named.

expectations.text: Explains the maturity model correctly: levels 0-3 with ML2 tightening scope and timeframes over ML1 (e.g., broader coverage, faster patching, phishing-resistant MFA expectations), giving per-strategy ML2 guidance without contradicting the model's structure
expectations.evidence: 'Each strategy has four maturity levels: ML0 (not implemented / not aligned), ML1, ML2, and ML3' — explicit, plus detailed per-strategy ML2 requirements (fortnightly scanning, 48-hour patch SLA, path+publisher/hash rules, phishing-resistant MFA noted as increasing toward ML3).

expectations.text: Maps each strategy to the relevant ISM control areas/chapters (system hardening, privileged access, authentication/MFA, patch management, backup and recovery) — mapping is directional and accurate, not invented control IDs
expectations.evidence: Table maps each strategy to a named control theme (application security/hardening, vulnerability/patch management, access control/IAM, authentication hardening, backup/BC) without inventing specific chapter numbers or control IDs, explicitly caveating 'exact chapter numbers shift between ISM revisions'.

expectations.text: Notes at least one accurate currency fact: none of the 2026-added ISM controls (including the June 2026 AI controls) carry Essential Eight mappings, and/or that E8 assessment expectations for Commonwealth entities sit under PSPF policy rather than the ISM itself
expectations.evidence: No mention of the 2026-added controls or their (lack of) Essential Eight mapping. The closest reference — 'incorporated directly into the ISM... as a mandated (for many Commonwealth entities, under PSPF Policy 10)' — conflates rather than clearly distinguishes PSPF-driven E8 mandate from ISM control content, so it does not clearly satisfy either currency fact.
